summary: Susan Meinheit is a tibetologist who held a post at the Library of Congress, attested in 1998 and 2007.

Susan Naquin studied at Stanford (BA 1962–1966) and Yale (MA 1968, PhD 1974). A historian and sinologist, she taught at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as professor at Princeton University from 1993 to 2013.

Susan Neiman earned her PhD from Harvard (1977–1986) and studied at the Free University of Berlin. A philosopher, she was a professor at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and became Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who held a post in the religion department at Amherst College around 1978.

Susan Whitfield completed her PhD at SOAS (1995). A scholar of sinology and Iranian/Central Asian history, she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor in Silk Road Studies at the University of East Anglia.

Susannah Deane earned degrees from Bangor, Bristol, and Cardiff (PhD 2015). Specializing in Buddhist studies and tibetology, she held teaching posts at several UK universities before becoming a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Bristol (2017–2021) and joining UWE in 2023.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph studied at Sarah Lawrence and Harvard/Radcliffe (PhD 1955). An indologist and political scientist, she taught at Harvard (1955–1963) and became a professor at the University of Chicago in 1964, later serving as APSA president (2003–2004).
Susanne Kerekes, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Trinity College, Hartford.

Susanne Mrozik studied at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986. Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and indology, he also served as a lecturer in Indian religions at the University of Birmingham.

Indologist Sushil Kumar De studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS (D.Litt. ~1921), and Bonn. He taught at Presidency, Calcutta, and Jadavpur, served as Professor of Sanskrit at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and held a post at Sanskrit College (~1951–1956).
Susmita Basu Majumdar studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta. She works in history, archaeology, and indology, and holds a post at the University of Calcutta.

Susumu Kajiura is a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He was an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and director of the humanities research department at Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property, attested in 2001.

Susumu Otake studied at the University of Tsukuba under Makio Takemura. Working in Buddhist studies and sinology, he held part-time lecturer positions at Kyoto University (attested 2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

Susumu Shimazono studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. A scholar of religious studies and japanology, he was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later taught at Sophia University (~2013–2019).

Susumu Winston Nakamura earned his MA at the University of California, Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing (~1934–1937). Specializing in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and japanology, he lectured at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1942–1946) and UC Berkeley.

Susumu Yamaguchi studied at Otani University, Kyoto University, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. An indologist, tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, he was a long-time professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri studied at London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto (PhD). A Buddhist studies scholar, he founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, and held posts at the University of Toronto and Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès studied at INALCO and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at EFEO (1922–1925, 1936–1941), conserved the National Library of Cambodia (1925–1936), and founded the Buddhist Institute in 1930.

Suzanne Newcombe studied at Amherst, LSE, and Cambridge (PhD 2008). Working in indology and religious studies, she held posts at Inform, LSE, Cambridge, and the Open University, and served as honorary director of Inform at King's College London (attested 2020).
